summary: Technical review of Module 01 (en). Recomputed every equation, derivation and number in sections 1-12, 'What goes wrong', the 15 exercises, the 12 quiz questions and the summary. Re-ran every concept and exercise code block that has an output (all match except e13's machine-dependent timings) and all five labs with labrun (ALL LABS MATCH). Independently recomputed with labpy: the s2 fit and noise RMS, the s3 eigenvalues and step-count table, the s4 floors including the decaying step's last-epoch mean (1.7e-5) and the with-replacement runs, the s8 bias-variance tables at N = 20 and 200, the learning-curve values and the N = 115 crossover, the double-descent values, the CV folds, the s9 ridge point at lambda = 0.032 (train 0.182, df 10.44, tau 0.38), E[Z_max] for 10/120/200/1200 draws, the McNemar p-values, the make_moons accuracies, the e13 fold statistics, the e14 refits and the Lab 2 step-size extension. Citations, cross-module anchors (M02 s1/s7/s8/s9/s11/s12, M03 s10, M05 s2, M06 s4/s11, M07 s1/s10, M08 s6), public-site rules, topic ownership (ECE in s7; SE, bootstrap and McNemar in s10; only pointers for momentum, Adam, Huber, temperature scaling and perplexity) and the CANONICAL star grades (e5 is ★★; e11, e12 and e15 are conceptual ★; 130 minutes) all check out. Quiz: each question has exactly one defensible answer once Q12's figure is corrected. Counts: 10 fixes in all. 4 are numerical or factual errors: the '95% interval of ±1%' on c1 (really ±1.9%; the 1% is the standard error) in three places, e15's '2ε is about 8% at 5% strain' (it is 10%), s8's 'less than one standard error', and s4's 'at or slightly above'. 6 are precision or reproducibility fixes: e5's ambiguous 'survive', e13's 'standard deviation of 0.07 in each', s11's threshold wording, the s11 make_moons settings, and the s4 and s8 numbers added in passing. There are 3 lab issues, reported and not edited. node tools/check.mjs --module 1 --lang en reports 0 errors and 0 warnings.
changes: 12-concepts-c.md s12 check: before 'The 95% interval of $c_1$ is $\pm1\%$, yet at 40% strain the neo-Hookean prediction is 13% off.' after 'The standard error of $c_1$ is 1% (a 95% interval of about $\pm2\%$), yet at 40% strain the neo-Hookean prediction is 13% off.' (SE/c1 = 0.0997/10.09 = 0.99%; 1.96 x SE = 1.94%.)
40-practice.md quiz Q12: before 'has a 95% interval of about $\pm1\%$ on $c_1$' after 'has a 95% interval of about $\pm2\%$ on $c_1$'. Same reason.
40-practice.md summary, last bullet: before 'A neo-Hookean fit with a $\pm1\%$ interval over 0–20% strain' after 'A neo-Hookean fit with a $\pm2\%$ 95% interval over 0–20% strain'.

30-exercises.md e15(b): before 'a relative difference of about $2\varepsilon$. Over 5% of strain that is about 8%, below what the noise lets the residuals show; over 20% it is large against the noise, the residuals form runs, ...' after 'a relative difference of about $2\varepsilon$. Over the first 5% of strain the ratio of the two branches runs from about 1.05 to 1.10; a single $c_1$ absorbs its average, and what is left, a few per cent across the range, is below what the noise lets the residuals show. Over 20% the ratio runs from 1.05 to 1.5, far more than one coefficient can absorb, the residuals form runs, ...' (2ε at ε = 0.05 is 10%; exact |g(0.95)|/g(1.05) = 1.105, and 1.508 at 20%.)

11-concepts-b.md s8 'Five folds on twenty points': before 'Cross-validation prefers degree 5 by 0.021, less than one standard error, while ...' after 'Cross-validation prefers degree 5 by 0.021, which is about one standard error of the fold-wise difference (the five differences have a standard error of 0.021), while ...' (0.021 exceeds degree 5's own SE of 0.016; the fold-wise difference is 1.03 standard errors.)

10-concepts-a.md s4 'Lab 1's floors': before 'with independently drawn batches the same runs land at or slightly above the prediction.' after 'with independently drawn batches the same runs land at or above the prediction, by up to about half again (2.0 against $1.4\times10^{-4}$ at $B = 32$).' (Measured with replacement, seed 1: 2.0e-4, 4.7e-4, 1.5e-3 and 4.3e-4 against 1.4e-4, 4.4e-4, 1.2e-3 and 4.0e-4.)

30-exercises.md e5(c): before 'the cracks that survive the first stage are the easy ones' after 'the cracks that the first stage flags are the easy ones'. ('Survive' reads as 'missed by', which reverses the argument.)

30-exercises.md e13: before 'The forest is a distant third at about 0.45 above boosting, with a standard deviation of 0.07 in each.' after '... at about 0.45 above boosting, against fold-to-fold standard deviations of 0.07 (forest) and 0.04 (boosting).' (Boosting's SD is 0.04, not 0.07.)

12-concepts-c.md s11 trees: before 'A threshold is unchanged by any monotone rescaling of its feature, so trees need no scaling.' after 'An increasing rescaling of a feature moves a threshold on it without changing which points fall on each side, so trees need no scaling.' (The threshold value does move; the partition does not. This now matches the section's own check answer.)

12-concepts-c.md s11 'Four classifiers on two moons': added the settings that reproduce the numbers: make_moons random_state=0, shuffled stratified folds with random_state=0, defaults with random_state=0 where a model takes one, and gradient boosting named as `HistGradientBoostingClassifier`. (GradientBoostingClassifier gives 0.953; the quoted 0.947 is HistGradientBoostingClassifier.)
issues: Lab 5, step 7 (21-labs-b.md lines 764-765): '\nu' was turned into a newline, leaving the broken math 'a $\chi^2_' + newline + 'u$ this low has a probability ...'. Fix: join the lines into 'with 14 degrees of freedom a $\chi^2_\nu$ this low has a probability of about 2.5% under a correct model.' (P(chi2_14 <= 5.6) = 0.024, so 2.5% is right.) check.mjs does not flag it.

Lab 3, step 2 (20-labs-a.md line 971-972): 'the even Legendre term added at degree 4 has almost no true coefficient'. On this symmetric design the even terms are exactly orthogonal to the odd target, as Section 8 says. Fix: 'has a true coefficient of exactly zero on this symmetric design, so it can only fit noise'.

Lab 1, step 5 (20-labs-a.md line 206-207): 'add 100 to the second, as if a temperature were recorded in kelvin rather than as a deviation'. Kelvin would add about 273, not 100. Fix: 'as if a temperature near 100 °C were recorded in °C rather than as a deviation from 100 °C'.

No source errors found in the citations. They were checked from knowledge, not on the web: Robbins and Monro 1951, Keskar et al. ICLR 2017, Guo et al. ICML 2017, Belkin et al. PNAS 2019, Nakkiran et al. ICLR 2020, Grinsztajn et al. NeurIPS D&B 2022, Wolpert 1996, McNemar 1947, Dietterich 1998, Kapoor and Narayanan Patterns 2023, Kaufman et al. TKDD 2012, Gent 1996 and the rest of the reference list. A web spot-check before publication would still be prudent.

Section 9's 'one-standard-error rule (Hastie et al., 2009)' credits the book that popularised the rule. The rule itself goes back to Breiman et al.'s CART (1984). Not changed, because the attribution as a reference for the rule is defensible.
